baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction "worships God on a harf" is followed by paired outcome clauses: good strikes him and he settles; trial strikes him and he turns on his face.
baseline_models.mechanism: Worship is held at a directionally susceptible margin. Incoming outcomes function as decision signals: benefit produces repose, assay produces reversal, and allowing either arrival to govern allegiance culminates in comprehensive deficit.

activation_trace.role: Submissive worship supplies the allegiance whose durability the paired conditions expose.
Inclination away from a direction makes the harf a posture poised for deflection.
Targeted arrival gives both good and trial the functional force of impacts reaching the worshipper.
Stillness marks the favorable outcome as temporary repose rather than demonstrated constancy.
Assay of metal or person makes adversity disclose the quality of the prior worship.
Turning a thing from face to face supplies the decisive reorientation under trial.
General diminution makes the doubled loss the resulting collapse across both named horizons.

changed_reading.before: A weak believer feels calm in prosperity and abandons worship in adversity.
changed_reading.after: An outcome-governed worshipper lets whatever reaches him set his direction: benefit quiets him, assay rotates him, and that contingent allegiance itself realizes loss.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The spatial chain "on a harf ... settles ... turns on his face" can be read as one continuous bodily mechanics.
baseline_models.mechanism: The worshipper occupies a sloping margin rather than a load-bearing stance. Favorable contact lets the body sink into provisional rest; adverse contact rolls its facing over, rendering doctrinal instability as failed bodily support.

activation_trace.role: The mountain-side comparison supplies a steep, precarious surface for the harf construction.
Downward movement turns the two arrivals into loads acting on the perched posture.
Physical lowering supplies the body's temporary settling under favorable load.
Rotation from one face to another supplies the loss of balance under adverse load.
Direction and destination make the fallen face an altered vector, not merely an injured body part.

changed_reading.before: The verse contrasts inner emotional calm with later apostasy.
changed_reading.after: The verse stages a body balanced on a slope: prosperity permits temporary settling, while trial rolls its facing over and exposes that it never possessed independent footing.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Harf, good, loss, the nearer world, and the later world form an economic and temporal cluster around worship.
baseline_models.mechanism: Worship is practiced like a short-horizon transaction or livelihood. Immediate good is treated as return; trial is treated as a failed deal; withdrawal then writes off both the near account and the deferred account.

activation_trace.role: Craft, earning, and transaction make the worshipper's harf an exchange-oriented mode of practice.
Useful good supplies the return by which the worshipper evaluates the relationship.
Commercial loss turns reversal into a failed exchange that consumes its capital.
Nearness gives the worldly account the immediacy favored by the worshipper's calculus.
Deferral to a later time supplies the second account that short-term evaluation discounts.

changed_reading.before: Turning away is followed by punishment in this life and the next.
changed_reading.after: The worship is already structured as a near-term bargain; exiting when immediate returns fail crystallizes a transaction that forfeits both present and deferred capital.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately following invocation scene externalizes where outcome-calculus leads. The worshipper who turns for utility enters a relation evaluated by harm and benefit, yet its harm is nearer than its benefit and its patronage and companionship are bad; the bargain is therefore not merely cancelled but transferred into a self-defeating allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Useful good supplies the payoff criterion operating in the focus ayah.
Trade loss supplies the negative balance that the next two ayat explain relationally.
Harm as the contrary of benefit makes expected utility an explicit criterion of the alternative invocation.
Benefit opposed to harm names the return the alternative object cannot supply.
Nearness makes harm, not benefit, the outcome closest to the transferred allegiance.
Patronage through support and allegiance turns the transaction into a governing relationship.
Interpersonal association makes the failed utility choice also a failed companionship.

structural_cues: 22:12-13 directly follow the focus and move from reversal and loss to invocation, harm, benefit, patron, and associate.
The near/far contrast in 22:12-13 echoes the focus ayah's near world and later world without repeating its exact temporal pair.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency and the explicit utility and patronage vocabulary; I infer that the next scene displays the destination and logic of the focus reversal. A live alternative is that 22:12-13 describes a generic polytheist rather than the identical person in 22:11.

changed_reading.before: The worshipper cancels a bargain with God when adversity makes it unprofitable.
changed_reading.after: The worshipper shops for a more useful allegiance, but the transfer selects nearer harm and corrupt patronage, so the loss is generated by the utility calculus itself.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later, the same arrival construction is attached to people who restrain themselves rather than turn. This creates a controlled contrast: being struck by an event does not dictate reversal; the event differentiates a patient stance from an outcome-dependent one.

activation_trace.role: A calamity taking a person supplies the adverse arrival that appears to precipitate reversal in the focus.
Turning from face to face supplies the focus response against which patience is contrasted.
The repeated adverse arrival holds the event type constant across the two response patterns.
Holding the self back from panic supplies the counter-response to face-first reversal.

structural_cues: 22:35 coordinates patience over what strikes them with hearts that tremble, established prayer, and giving from provision.
The recurrence of the ص و ب arrival construction makes response, rather than event class, the primary variable.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated root and construction plus patience in 22:35; I infer a deliberate counter-response that removes causal necessity from adversity-to-reversal. Alternatively, the recurrence may simply describe a separate virtuous group without directly glossing 22:11.

changed_reading.before: Trial causes the marginal worshipper to reverse.
changed_reading.after: The same kind of impact can be held with patience, so trial is a differentiating occasion and the loss arises from the worshipper's response, not from affliction alone.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later fitna sequence locates divergent responses in heart material. Trial becomes an assay for diseased or hardened hearts, while recognition of truth lets other hearts become like low, tranquil ground and enter a straight path. The focus ayah's visible turn on the face is thus the exterior motion of an interior terrain that cannot receive the assay steadily.

activation_trace.role: Assay of metal or person supplies the diagnostic event in the focus.
Face-to-face rotation supplies the outward movement whose interior basis the context exposes.
The repeated assay explicitly targets differentiated human interiors.
Heart as understanding and inner faculty identifies the substrate being tested.
Departure from health and balance supplies one defective condition revealed by fitna.
Loss of the heart's softness supplies the second unreceptive condition.
The receptive heart provides the contrasting interior outcome of the same sequence.
Low, tranquil, open ground gives the receptive heart a stable terrain image opposite the precarious edge.
A straight road supplies the directed course reached by the receptive heart.
Straightness and balanced alignment make the path the structural opposite of turning on a margin.

structural_cues: 22:53-54 place fitna and two kinds of heart response in consecutive opposed clauses.
22:54 joins heart receptivity to guidance along a straight path, linking interior condition to directional outcome.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fitna, diseased and hard hearts, receptive hearts, tranquil terrain, and straight direction; I infer that the focus's bodily reversal reveals its heart substrate. A live alternative is that 22:53-54 concerns reception of a communicated sign rather than the personal good/adversity pair of 22:11.

changed_reading.before: External outcomes toggle the worshipper's surface behavior.
changed_reading.after: Fitna assays the heart's material: a diseased or hardened interior expresses itself as face-turning, while a receptive, level interior settles into a straight course.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus is embedded in a directional sequence. A bent side leads away from God's road before it; guidance to a path follows later. Harf, turning, face, side, road, and path jointly make unstable worship a negotiable bodily vector rather than merely low conviction.

activation_trace.role: Inclination away from direction makes the worship posture vulnerable to a route change.
Face as direction and destination gives reversal an orientational consequence.
Folding and diverting supplies the bodily change immediately preceding the focus.
Turning the side away gives the preceding figure an embodied refusal posture.
A traversable extended road supplies the direction from which the bent posture diverts others.
Gentle direction to a road and truth supplies the positive alternative to impact-driven turning.
The straight path supplies the stable route absent from worship on a deflecting margin.

structural_cues: 22:9 and 22:11 place side-bending, a divine road, worship on a harf, and turning on a face within three consecutive ayat.
22:24 answers the earlier diversion with repeated guidance to a path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency and repeated body-and-route vocabulary; I infer a shared directional field in which bodily posture indexes allegiance. Alternatively, 22:9 and 22:11 may intentionally present separate human types rather than phases of one directional mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Harf names generic wavering or marginal commitment.
changed_reading.after: Harf locates worship in a route geometry: the body can perform worship while its facing remains negotiable, and trial exposes the direction it actually takes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens by shaking the ground, later pictures a body falling from the sky and being swept away, and finally names the sky as actively held from falling. Stability therefore cannot mean that conditions never move; it means dependence on what holds them. The edge worshipper mistakes favorable local equilibrium for ultimate support.

activation_trace.role: Lowering into rest supplies the worshipper's condition-dependent equilibrium.
Physical overturning supplies the local failure of support.
Shaking and oscillation make environmental stability unavailable as a final foundation from the surah's opening.
A turbulent sounding fall supplies the uncontrolled trajectory of lost allegiance.
Descent into an abyss extends face-turning into unarrested spatial loss.
Wind and moving air supply the external force that carries an unsupported body away.
Active holding supplies the support that keeps the sky from completing its possible fall.
Falling followed by fixed contact names the cosmic motion being restrained.

structural_cues: 22:1, 22:31, and 22:65 distribute shaking, falling, sweeping, and holding across the whole surah.
The focus ayah's settling and overturning form a human-scale version of this larger support vocabulary.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the motion and holding images; I infer that divine holding, rather than favorable circumstances, is the implied stable support for the focus worshipper. Alternatively, the cosmic images may frame divine power without specifying the psychology of 22:11.

changed_reading.before: The worshipper fails because adversity destabilizes his environment.
changed_reading.after: A moving world is expected; the failure is treating temporary equilibrium as support and losing relation to the holder when conditions shift.

context_deltas.mechanism: Whole-surah ritual economy permits real benefits but refuses to make them payment to God. Benefits are witnessed, provision is named, consumed, and passed to the poor; flesh and blood do not reach God, while protective God-consciousness does. Good can therefore be received without becoming the criterion of worship when it is circulated toward remembrance and care.

activation_trace.role: Useful good supplies the received benefit that the focus worshipper treats as payment.
Earning and transaction supply the bargain model revised by the ritual economy.
Presence with witnessing makes benefits occasions of conscious participation rather than private payout.
Benefit as the contrary of harm confirms that the ritual setting contains genuine utility.
Vocal remembrance redirects benefit toward naming God.
Allotted gift makes material good entrusted provision rather than contractual wage.
Feeding another gives provision an outward distributive route.
Reaching a target distinguishes material offerings that do not arrive from the inward quality that does.
Placing the self in protection supplies the inward orientation that reaches beyond the commodity.

structural_cues: 22:28 sequences benefits, remembrance, allotted provision, eating, and feeding the poor.
22:37 explicitly denies that flesh or blood reaches God and contrasts them with taqwa.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies benefit, provision, distribution, and the contrast over what reaches God; I infer that these regulate how received good should function in 22:11. A live alternative is that the focus's good is broader than the sacrificial and pilgrimage benefits of 22:28-37.

changed_reading.before: Good received from God is the wage that keeps the worship bargain active.
changed_reading.after: Good is entrusted provision: it can be witnessed, remembered, consumed, and shared without becoming payment, because inward protective orientation rather than the commodity is what reaches God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah's closing command reverses the focus ayah's agency. The edge worshipper waits for good to strike him before settling; the addressed believers are commanded to worship and enact good. Good moves from incoming condition to outgoing practice, displacing receipt as the measure of allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Targeted arrival makes the focus worshipper the recipient on whom good lands.
Useful good supplies the incoming condition for continued worship.
Commanded submissive worship restores worship as an action rather than a reaction to payout.
Bringing an act into being makes the addressee the producer of good.
The same useful good becomes the object of commanded action rather than an arriving benefit.

structural_cues: 22:77 coordinates bowing, prostrating, worshipping, and doing good in imperative form.
The same ع ب د and خ ي ر roots recur at the surah's close with reversed grammatical agency.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the shared roots and the recipient-versus-agent constructions; I infer a thematic answer in which producing good displaces waiting for good. Alternatively, the closing imperative may be a general exhortation whose agency contrast with 22:11 is incidental.

changed_reading.before: The worshipper remains active only while good arrives to him.
changed_reading.after: Stable worship coordinates devotion with causing good to exist; the worshipper's role changes from payoff-recipient to responsible agent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's near and later accounts are recalibrated by a surah that opposes haste to promise, stretches a day to a thousand counted years, makes the Hour arrive suddenly, and places good provision after killing or death. Immediate conditions cannot display the final balance; edge worship mistakes delay for absence and present adversity for completed accounting.

activation_trace.role: Nearness supplies the immediate horizon preferred by contingent worship.
Deferral supplies the later horizon that cannot be valued from one present impact.
Haste and premature demand expose the pressure to collapse promise into immediate result.
Promise opens expectation beyond what the current moment visibly pays.
A temporal duration that can exceed ordinary counting expands the accounting horizon.
Sudden arrival prevents delay from being read as non-arrival.
Allotted gift after migration, killing, or death places good beyond immediate worldly survival.

structural_cues: 22:47 contrasts demands for haste with an unfailing promise and radically different temporal scale.
22:55 gives the delayed event sudden arrival, while 22:58 locates provision after death as well as after migration.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies near/later vocabulary, haste, promise, expanded duration, suddenness, and post-death provision; I infer temporal myopia as a mechanism of edge worship. Alternatively, these eschatological timings may frame the surah globally without specifically explaining the focus person's decision.

changed_reading.before: The worshipper loses two separate domains after one bad response.
changed_reading.after: The two domains are one extended account whose balance cannot be inferred from immediate arrivals; reversal is a premature closing of the books.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading unexpectedly imports the rope-and-cut mechanics of 22:15 into the focus's edge posture. It remains anchored by harf, reversal, loss, the shared world/later pair, and the nearby support vocabulary, but downstream prose should present it only as a spatial analogy, not as a lexical gloss or a claim that both ayat describe one literal act.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The worshipper stands on a harf, turns on his face, and loses both the world and the later life.

activation_trace.role: The mountain-side image supplies the precarious location from which support matters.
Comprehensive diminution supplies the result of losing support.
Aid and visible support supply the expectation whose apparent absence provokes the act.
Drawing something lengthwise until it connects supplies an extended support line.
A rope and connection make support materially severable.
Termination and loss of connection supply the self-severing action.

changed_reading.before: The worshipper is defeated when hoped-for support does not appear.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, reversal resembles cutting the very line that could hold an edge-dweller, so the loss is self-severed support rather than simple external defeat.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain reading carries fitna's metallurgical branch into the later melting and iron imagery. It remains valid as an assay model anchored in the focus's fitna and reversal, but the later heat scenes concern punishment; downstream prose must qualify the connection as material analogy rather than claim that the focus trial is literally fire or metalwork.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: A fitna strikes the worshipper and the person turns on his face.

activation_trace.role: Testing metal and person supplies the focus event as an assay of composition.
The thing's core or pure interior supplies what the assay is imagined to disclose.
Melting by heat supplies the material process that exposes whether an interior holds.
Iron hardness supplies the contrasting material property within the assay analogy.

changed_reading.before: Fitna is simply an adverse circumstance that changes the person's decision.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, fitna heats and tests the worship's inner material; the face-turn is the deformation that reveals what the apparently settled posture was made of.

strongest_changes: The repeated impact construction in 22:35 pairs what strikes a person with patience, showing that adversity does not mechanically cause reversal.
The fitna-and-hearts sequence in 22:53-54 turns the focus's outward face-flip into an assay of interior terrain and receptivity.
The closing command in 22:77 reverses good from something received as a condition of worship into something the worshipper is ordered to enact.
Whole-surah shaking, falling, path, and holding imagery recasts harf as a support-and-direction problem rather than only weak conviction.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet activated a coherent mechanics of arrival, support, direction, assay, and agency: edge worship evaluates what comes in, while stable worship governs its response, circulates provision, and causes good to go out.
remaining_uncertainties: The harf inventory emphasizes inclination, mountain-side comparison, and transaction more than an explicit lexical edge, so some spatial detail rests on the focus construction plus reader mapping.
The sequence supports linking the figures in 22:9 and 22:12-13 to the mechanism of 22:11, but it does not explicitly identify them as the same person.
The receive-good/do-good contrast may be thematic recurrence rather than a deliberate grammatical answer.
The rope and thermal outliers remain analogical and should not be rendered as lexical senses.
